task.name: Rates are declared in two places, one of which no configuration can override, so the catalog is authoritative only until the compiled fallback is consulted
task.story_text:
## Why

Rates are still declared in two places. The catalog is the operator-facing one — data, editable
without a release, carrying provenance for every figure. The other is a dictionary compiled into the
runner package, which nobody outside a release can change and which no configuration can override.

The resolution mechanism that made the catalog authoritative has already landed. Pricing is compiled
once at configuration load into a registry keyed by the dispatched identity, and every accounting
site looks up what actually ran rather than what it was seated as. The compiled dictionary survives
only as a fallback for the case where no registry is installed.

What it still holds is a prior generation. Of its 21 entries, 10 duplicate models the catalog already
prices, and the remaining 11 are older families that nothing currently enables. So the second source
of truth persists to serve models nobody dispatches, while continuing to be a place where a rate can
disagree with the catalog and win by being consulted second.

Three catalog entries carry no rate at all and are not covered by the dictionary either, so they are
unpriced everywhere. One of them is a cheap-tier entry the router actively prefers, which makes it
the most likely of the three to be selected and the most likely to produce an unmeasurable run.

Two catalog entries also carry no rate deliberately and should keep none: their transport returns a
billed figure rather than token counts, so a rate card is never consulted for them. That distinction
belongs in the catalog as a stated property rather than as an absence a reader has to infer.

## Example

Where a rate can be declared today, and what each place holds:

```
catalog (data, per-entry provenance, overridable)     19 entries priced
compiled dictionary (code, release-only, no override) 21 entries
  ├─ 10 duplicate the catalog
  └─ 11 exist only here — all prior-generation, none enabled

unpriced in both:
  deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner     token-returning transport, genuinely need rates
  gemini-3-flash-preview               cheap tier, cost_rank 1 — the router prefers it

unpriced on purpose:
  claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5       transport returns billed dollars; no rate is consulted
```

Wanted: one place. A rate is declared in the catalog or overridden in project configuration, and an
entry that needs no rate says so rather than looking identical to one that is missing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A rate is declared in exactly one kind of place, which an operator can edit without a release and
  override per project, so two sources cannot disagree about what a dispatch costs.
- Every model that a token-returning transport can dispatch has a rate reachable from that single
  source, so no enabled identity is unpriced by construction.
- An entry whose transport returns a billed figure rather than token counts records that as a stated
  property, so "needs no rate" is distinguishable from "rate is missing" without inferring it from an
  absent field.
- Rates that exist only to serve identities nothing can dispatch are either carried into the single
  source with their provenance, or removed with a record of what was dropped, so the migration does
  not silently lose pricing for a model someone later enables.
- After the change, no accounting path consults a rate that configuration could not have supplied.
- Behaviour is unchanged for every identity priced correctly today, including those measured through
  a self-reporting transport.

## Out of scope

Changing how a resolved rate is looked up at dispatch, or what an unpriced identity does at runtime.
That mechanism landed separately and this issue removes the second source it still falls back to,
rather than altering it.

handoff.summary: Removed PRICING_TABLE, the packaged rate dictionary in runners/rate_registry.py, and the compile-time legacy materialization in config/dispatch_rates.py that widened its transport-agnostic rows onto concrete dispatch identities (plus the RateSource.LEGACY_COMPAT variant and the per-transport-conflict plumbing that existed only to police that widening). compile_rate_registry now builds entries from the merged model registry alone, so every figure in a compiled registry came from config/data/models.yaml or forge.yaml. The two remaining packaged-table readers were re-pointed at the shipped catalog: schema_utils.pricing_for is now catalog-only (the no-registry baseline), and runner_claude's kill-path reconstruction sources both its anthropic CLI name set and its last-resort rates from schema_utils.catalog_rates() — the billed ids it resolves (claude-opus-4-6, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5) are pinned catalog entries carrying identical figures with pricing_provenance, so those paths are numerically unchanged. Added a cost.rate_basis catalog field (token_rates default, provider_reported) plumbed through pricing.py, AgentSpec (with a uses_rate_card property), the parser and both resolution modes; claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5 declare provider_reported. It is enforced, not decorative: parse refuses provider_reported alongside per-MTok figures, an overlay that declares figures flips the basis back to token_rates, and _spec_rates/_catalog_rates return no rate card for a provider_reported spec even if figures were inherited. The 11 orphaned rows are recorded in docs/reference/dropped-legacy-rates.md with their figures and a re-enable recipe; the 10 duplicated rows are documented as already carried by catalog entries.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 ('changing the no-registry baseline may expose callers that relied on the packaged fallback') is only partly retired. The plan's Step 2 detail for runner_claude.py mentions only 'preserve provider-reported cost handling', but the actual PRICING_TABLE consumer there is the token-estimation kill path: _anthropic_cli_pricing_names (runner_claude.py:173-185) unions PRICING_TABLE's anthropic keys into known_models('anthropic','cli') to build the prefix-match name set, and _estimate_anthropic_cost (runner_claude.py:220-235) reads PRICING_TABLE as a last-resort packaged fallback. With no registry installed (unit tests, non-config processes) known_models returns nothing, so deleting the table without a replacement name source makes _resolve_anthropic_pricing_key return None and _reconstruct_partial_cost silently degrade to cost-unknown — a behaviour regression against the last acceptance criterion.
  Suggestion: In Step 2, explicitly source the anthropic CLI name set and last-resort rates from schema_utils.catalog_rates() (which already carries claude-opus-4-6, claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-haiku-4-5 with pricing_provenance, verified equal to the table figures) rather than dropping the fallback outright. Note that rate_registry.py is enforced as an import leaf by tests/test_dispatch_rate_registry.py:~925, so any catalog-derived helper belongs in schema_utils, not rate_registry.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's test file list omits tests/test_runner_claude.py, which directly exercises the code Step 2 changes: _reconstruct_partial_cost is asserted at tests/test_runner_claude.py:985, 1002, 1010 and 1017. These run without an installed registry and today get their prices from the packaged table.
  Suggestion: Add tests/test_runner_claude.py to Step 3 and re-point those assertions at catalog-sourced rates.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 says to 'change no-registry behavior to fail through validation/runtime paths already used for missing pricing rather than silently consulting compiled defaults.' schema_utils.pricing_for is documented (schema_utils.py:301-317) as a deliberately-unchanged transport-blind baseline, and entry_for's fallback to it is explicitly out of scope per the spec ('Changing how a resolved rate is looked up at dispatch... landed separately'). Two existing tests pin it: tests/test_dispatch_rate_registry.py:657 (test_uninstalled_registry_reproduces_pricing_for_exactly) and :940 (schema_utils.PRICING_TABLE is rate_registry.PRICING_TABLE).
  Suggestion: Keep pricing_for and the entry_for baseline; the only change needed is deleting its second lookup (schema_utils.py:322) so it returns catalog rates or None. Update the :940 re-export assertion rather than removing the baseline mechanism.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (stale spec examples) is retired by the plan's mitigation, and I confirmed the staleness concretely: gemini-3-flash-preview is already priced in the catalog with pricing_provenance (models.yaml:447-457 API, :513-524 CLI), and deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner are catalog entries deliberately carrying no cost block as retired identifiers. Only the PRICING_TABLE duplication/orphan half of the spec is live work.
  Suggestion: Derive the migration list from the current catalog as the mitigation already states; do not add rates for the three identities the spec's Example block lists as unpriced.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
